title: Muhammad Azani Hasibuan
text:
Hi, I’m Azan — a lecturer in Information Systems and a PhD candidate in Computer Science, with a passion for learning analytics, educational technology, and intelligent systems that empower learners.
Over the past few years, I’ve dedicated myself to exploring how data can enhance education. My current research focuses on developing a framework to transform low-level student activity logs into meaningful behavioral insights, helping educators better understand and support self-regulated learning in digital environments. I combine expertise in process mining, machine learning, and behavioral analytics to bridge the gap between raw educational data and impactful learning decisions.
As a lecturer, I love designing student-centered learning experiences using real-world case studies, mastery-based learning models, and active learning strategies. I’ve taught courses in Object-Oriented Programming, Databases, and Information Systems Strategy, and I always aim to make abstract concepts more approachable and applicable.
Beyond academia, I enjoy building personal productivity systems that integrate Islamic values with modern frameworks like OKR and the 12-Week Year. I also have hands-on experience with cloud computing (Azure, AWS), data visualization, and educational software development.

title: Muhammad Azani Hasibuan
text:
📘 Current Project
Dissertation Title:
A Systematic Framework for Context and Domain-Driven Event Abstraction in Multi-modal Data within Online Collaborative Learning Environments
Goal:
To measure and improve students’ self-regulation strategies by transforming raw learning events into high-level, interpretable learning actions — validated through expert judgment and process analysis.
